title: Known-issues publication criteria (definition, validation, ownership)
creator: Chris Osei
project: CS&S Escalation Playbook Refresh + Known-Issues Sprint (Feb 2026)
description:
## Context
Support/CS is running a known-issues sprint to reduce repeat tickets and shorten time-to-mitigation. We need a clear, enforceable definition of what qualifies as a “Known Issue” (vs. “Troubleshooting” vs. “Incident/Status Page”), including validation requirements, how we label temporary workarounds vs permanent fixes, and who owns ongoing updates.

This ticket defines the publication criteria + review/ownership model so Support can publish consistently without leaking customer-sensitive details, and Engineering/SRE can trust what’s published.

## Goals
- Standardize what we publish as a Known Issue across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Require lightweight but real validation (repro evidence and/or telemetry signal) before publishing.
- Make workaround guidance copy/paste-ready and safe for customers.
- Clarify ownership and update responsibilities (no “write and forget”).
- Align with incident response: Known Issues should not replace status page updates when appropriate.

## Non-goals / out of scope
- Long-form root cause analysis (postmortems remain in incident tooling / internal docs).
- Roadmap commitments (“Fix ETA”) unless confirmed via Engineering issue and release train.
- Publishing customer-identifiable details (account names, specific IPs, internal hostnames, screenshots showing customer data).

---

## Definitions
### “Known Issue”
A recurring or high-impact customer-facing problem where:
1) Redwood has high confidence the symptom pattern is real (not a one-off customer misconfig), AND
2) there is a validated workaround or mitigation that reduces impact OR a clear “when to escalate” rule, AND
3) publishing guidance will reduce time-to-triage/mitigation and/or deflect repeat tickets.

Known Issues live in the Support/Help Center Known-Issues hub and are linkable from Support macros and ticket workflows.

### “Troubleshooting article” (not a Known Issue)
General guidance that applies broadly (timeouts, retries, auth setup) without asserting a platform defect or active regression.

### “Incident / degradation”
Active service issue that should follow incident process (#incidents, on-call, and possibly status page). A Known Issue may exist for the underlying class of problem, but it does not substitute for incident comms.

---

## Publication criteria (must meet)
A candidate must meet ALL of the following:
1) **Customer impact threshold**
   - Either (a) repeated tickets (e.g., ≥3 related tickets in a rolling 30 days), OR (b) at least one Sev0/Sev1 customer impact event, OR (c) materially increases Support time-to-triage (frequent back-and-forth for missing diagnostics), OR (d) impacts an enterprise/Dedicated/Private customer with contractual expectations (even if low volume).

2) **Pattern clarity**
   - Symptoms are describable in concrete terms (error codes/messages, observed behavior, affected endpoints).
   - Affected scope can be bounded (tier, region, model family, SDK versions, runtime version) OR explicitly marked as “Scope still being confirmed” with a conservative escalate rule.

3) **Validation evidence (minimum bar)**
   Must have at least ONE of:
   - Repro steps in a controlled environment (internal) OR customer-provided minimal repro validated by Support/Eng.
   - Observability signal from dashboards/logs that correlates with the symptom (error-rate spike, streaming reset metric, queue depth, pipeline lag).
   - Engineering/SRE confirmation in writing (comment/Slack summary) that the issue class is understood enough to publish mitigation + escalation triggers.

4) **Mitigation quality**
   Must include at least ONE of:
   - A workaround customers can apply safely (config change, retry/backoff guidance, known-good settings).
   - A Redwood-side mitigation Support/SRE can apply (feature flag, routing policy, capacity action) described at a high level (customer-safe), plus exactly when to escalate to trigger it.

5) **Safety + sensitivity**
   - No customer names, account IDs, request payloads containing secrets, or screenshots/logs with PII.
   - No internal-only tooling instructions that would expose sensitive controls. If needed, include “Support-only verification steps” in an internal-only section (or link internal runbook).

6) **Owner assigned**
   - Must have a named DRI responsible for accuracy and updates.

---

## Classification and labeling
Every Known Issue must be labeled with one of these lifecycle states:
- **Workaround Available (Temporary)**
  - We have mitigation steps, but underlying issue is not fully fixed or fix is not yet broadly deployed.
  - Must include: “Temporary workaround” callout and “Re-evaluate by” date (default: 30 days).

- **Workaround Available (Long-term / Recommended practice)**
  - Guidance is expected to remain valid even after fixes (e.g., client retry/idempotency best practices).
  - Should be considered for SDK docs integration.

- **Fix In Progress**
  - There is a linked Engineering issue with owner and status. Do not publish an ETA unless release is confirmed.
  - Must include: what changes once fixed (customer-visible behavior).

- **Fixed**
  - Fix is deployed and verified. Article should be updated to:
    - Mark fixed, include deployed version/region rollout info (if applicable), and
    - Keep a brief “What to do if you still see this” section with escalation triggers.
  - After 14–30 days, consider archiving or converting to Troubleshooting if it remains educational.

- **Monitoring / Under Investigation** (use sparingly)
  - Only allowed if there is high customer impact and Support needs a canonical place to capture current guidance.
  - Must have a strict escalate rule and a next-update date.

Required tags:
- Tier: hosted | dedicated | private
- Surface: api | sdk | console | routing | auth | audit-logs | billing | installer | autoscaling (choose all that apply)
- Region/model if applicable
- Recency tag: last-updated YYYY-MM-DD

---

## Required article sections (template)
1) **Summary (1–2 sentences)**
2) **Symptoms**
   - What the customer sees (errors, behaviors)
3) **Impact**
   - Who is affected; what breaks; severity guidance
4) **Affected configurations**
   - Tier/region/model/SDK/runtime versions; “unknown” allowed if called out clearly
5) **Workaround / Mitigation**
   - Step-by-step; include safe defaults; note risks
6) **Verification**
   - How to confirm mitigation worked (customer-observable signals)
7) **When to escalate**
   - Concrete triggers; what to include in escalation (request IDs, timestamps, region, model, SDK version)
8) **Status / Fix tracking**
   - Link to internal engineering issue (and public note if appropriate)
9) **Last updated + owner**

---

## Review and approval model
### Required reviewers before publish
- **Support SME** (e.g., Owen Phillips or Dev Patel delegate): ensures ticket alignment + macros.
- **Engineering or SRE validator** based on area:
  - Runtime/Serving/Latency/Streaming: SRE (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes) or Runtime on-call delegate
  - Dedicated autoscaling/capacity: SRE + Dedicated Eng delegate
  - Private installer/upgrades: Private Deployments/Platform delegate
  - Auth/SSO/Audit logs/Quota headers: Platform delegate
- **Docs/DevEx** (Elliot Price or assigned writer): style, clarity, customer-safe language, cross-links.
- **Security/Compliance** (Naomi Feldman) only if content touches Private/on-prem guidance, audit logs, or security posture claims.

### Approval mechanics
- Draft in Drive (or PR branch) → reviewer sign-off in ticket comments → publish to docs/Confluence.
- Any disagreements on “Known Issue vs Troubleshooting” go to Support lead + SRE partner for tie-break within 24 hours.

---

## Ongoing ownership and maintenance
- Each Known Issue has a DRI responsible for:
  - Updating within 2 business days of meaningful new info (new workaround, change in scope, fix rolled out).
  - Checking the article at least every 30 days while in Temporary/Investigating state.
- If no owner is available, the article must be unlisted (internal-only) until ownership is assigned.

## Linkage requirements
- Support macros must link to the Known Issue article (not a Drive draft).
- Support tickets (Jira SUP) should reference the Known Issue when applicable (to measure deflection/impact).
- Engineering tickets should be linked from the Known Issue for fix tracking.

## Metrics (what we’ll measure)
- Ticket deflection: decrease in repeat tickets for published issues (baseline vs post-publish 2–4 weeks).
- Time-to-triage: reduced back-and-forth for required diagnostics.
- Time-to-mitigation for escalations where a Known Issue exists.

## Deliverable
A published, team-aligned criteria doc + template that the known-issues sprint uses for all articles in batch 1.
acceptance_criteria:
- Criteria document approved by Support lead (Dev Patel), SRE partner (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes), and Docs lead (Elliot Price).
- Includes: definition, validation bar, lifecycle labels, required sections/template, reviewer/DRI model.
- Explicit guidance on sensitivity (what not to include) and incident/status-page boundary.
- Adopted by known-issues sprint: at least 3 articles published using this template with consistent labels and “when to escalate” sections.
decision_log:
- Decision: “Known Issue” requires validation evidence (repro OR observability OR Eng/SRE confirmation) before publish; no purely anecdotal publication.
- Decision: Allow “Monitoring/Under Investigation” only for high-impact cases with next-update date; otherwise keep as internal draft.
- Decision: No fix ETA language unless release is confirmed; link internal engineering issue for tracking.
- Decision: Every article must include “When to escalate” with required diagnostics to reduce on-call ping-pong.
rollout_plan:
1) Share criteria link in #support and #docs; ask writers to migrate existing drafts to template.
2) Update Support macros library to reference Known-Issues hub and new tagging.
3) During sprint review, reject any article missing validation or ownership.
4) Post-sprint: audit last-updated + owner fields; archive stale Temporary items or assign DRIs.

comments: 2026-02-03 (Chris Osei): Drafted initial criteria based on top ticket themes (streaming disconnects, 429/quota headers, Dedicated autoscaling oscillation, Private upgrade migrations, audit log lag). Requesting SRE + Support + Docs review by EOW to unblock publishing batch 1.

2026-02-04 (Dev Patel): +1 on requiring a minimal validation bar. Support can’t publish something we can’t confidently stand behind. Please add explicit wording on ‘customer-safe’ vs ‘Support-only verification’ steps; we’ve had folks paste internal dashboard links to customers in the past.

2026-02-05 (Sean Gallagher): Criteria looks good; one change: make sure Known Issues don’t become a substitute for incident comms. Add a callout: if error-rate/latency breach meets incident threshold, use incident process + status page guidelines; the known-issue article can be referenced but doesn’t replace comms cadence.

2026-02-06 (Elliot Price): From Docs POV, the required sections are right. Please add a strict requirement that every workaround includes a verification step and an ‘if you still see this’ escalation trigger. Otherwise we get KB pages that create more tickets.

2026-02-07 (Priya Natarajan): Platform ownership boundary: quota/rate-limit headers, audit log pipeline, SSO/SAML are Platform-reviewed before publish. Happy with the reviewer list; include Security review only when we make security posture claims or include Private/on-prem commands.

2026-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Added note re: ‘Monitoring/Under Investigation’ state: must include next-update date and conservative escalation trigger. Otherwise this state lingers and confuses on-call. Approved with that tweak.

2026-02-14 (Chris Osei): Finalized template + lifecycle labels after publish-review meeting. Marking Done. Next: ensure DES-233/ENG-4826 implement tags (tier/surface/region/model + last-updated) and Support macros link to the hub.
